card.name: Start of an article's opening sentence
card.fires_on: Early in a web article or headline, right after the opening topic phrase, on the noun, verb, comma or period that follows the subject. The subject is often a general topic such as a disease, ecosystem or country.

modes.label: After topic noun
modes.description: The word right after a short opening subject, such as a plural noun or a verb like is or are.
modes.example: Coastal ecosystems<< are>> vulnerable to habitat loss from impacts such as

modes.label: Sentence end in lead
modes.description: A period closing a short first or second sentence of an article.
modes.example: The internet is a large place<<.>> Billions of users access and create sites

modes.label: Topic term in title
modes.description: A word within a title-like opening phrase on a general topic.
modes.example: Chronic<< diseases>> such as asthma, arthritis, cancer,

card.writes: Weakly favors Chinese phrases meaning "there are many" and similar; the effect is unclear.
card.plain: It fires on the first few words of a general-interest article, just after the topic is named.
